channel.title: North Wales Chronicle - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from North Wales Chronicle (northwaleschronicle.co.uk)

item.title: Rail works in February for track upgrade between Pwllheli and Dovey Junction
item.description: Rail passengers are being urged to check before they travel due to major improvement works.

item.title: Anglesey girl Chloe Milloy to appear on S4C's Help Llaw
item.description: Ten-year-old Chloe Milloy from Bryngwran, Anglesey will appear in the opening episode of the second series of S4C’s Help Llaw, a children’s show featuring young people with additional needs.

item.title: YCYC set to hand out £60,000 to local projects
item.description: A funding scheme supporting grassroots projects has opened for applications.

item.title: Babyface brings wrestling and full‑blown camp to the Storyhouse stage
item.description: A riotous new musical from Anglesey writer Seiriol Davies is about to body‑slam its way onto the Storyhouse stage, blending full‑throttle musical theatre with live pro wrestling in a queer coming‑of‑age tale rooted in Rhyl, family legend and the fight to be yourself.

item.title: LOOK: Huge sinkhole causes section of Wales Coast Path in Gwynedd to close
item.description: A section of the Wales Coast Path in Gwynedd has closed after a huge sinkhole swallowed a section of the popular walking route.

item.title: South v North Wales - where is more beautiful? New Sky TV series reignites debate
item.description: Welsh presenter Alex Jones and actor Rafe Spall have reignited the argument about which location is more beautiful - South or North Wales?

item.title: From Lyons to Jones Bros and Mario Kreft: North Wales families on Rich List 2025
item.description: The combined fortunes of Wales’s 50 wealthiest individuals and families is now calculated at £10.5bn in this year’s Rich List - up 3.4 per cent on a year ago.

item.title: Housing plan for 48 homes at sensitive site near Penrhyn Castle moves toward approval
item.description: A major 48‑home affordable estate beside the grounds of Penrhyn Castle is heading to committee, with planners saying the sensitive site can be developed without harming the historic landscape.

item.title: WATCH: Jules Peters and son Evan perform Walk Forever at 32nd Gathering
item.description: Jules said she felt her husband’s presence in the moment and felt inspired by the optimism and energy that Mike always brought to life and to his music.

item.title: Pods, yurt and caravan plan refused over ‘harm’ to Anglesey beauty spot
item.description: A glamping project touted as low‑impact has been turned down by Anglesey Council, which said it would harm the AONB and lacked evidence on wildlife and flood safety.
